form.keywords: security, scanner, mcp, agent, skill, prompt-injection, supply-chain, sbom, sarif
form.short_description: AIShield is a local-first, open-source security scanner for MCP servers, Agent Skills, and AI tooling configurations. 235 MCP rules + 262 Skill rules. Covers OWASP MCP Top 10 + OWASP Agentic AI Top 10. Never-executes invariant: scanned configs are never run.
form.long_description:
AIShield is a local-first, open-source AI tool security scanner covering OWASP MCP Top 10 + OWASP Agentic AI Top 10 + sandbox hardening. 235 MCP rules + 262 Skill rules (including 27 SKILL_EXTRA for supply-chain / context-hijack / harness meta-abilities / memory poisoning / Chinese variants / benchmark claims / desktop driver / Agent payment & budget attack surface).

Core invariant: the scanner NEVER EXECUTES any command found in a scanned configuration. Many comparable tools actually start the scanned service to read tools/list — that means getting compromised before the health check. AIShield only reads files and issues HTTP audit requests. Zero subprocess, zero scanned-code execution surface.

What's included:
- Skill: skills/aishield-security-scan/SKILL.md — teaches agents to use AIShield to scan MCP servers, AI Skills, and Agent workspaces
- MCP Server: npx aishield-mcp-server — mounts the scanner as an MCP tool into Claude Code
- Output: CycloneDX SBOM + SARIF, drops directly into GitHub Code Scanning

Compliance statement: this is a DETECTION tool. Attack strings appearing in SKILL.md (like curl | sh) are patterns AIShield matches against — they are the scanned target, not instructions to the agent. The ruleset itself (scanner/rules.py) is stored as static regex+severity and is never interpreted as instructions at runtime. The MCP server is a pure HTTP client with no code execution surface.

License: MIT
form.self_audit_statement:
This plugin is a security scanner and does not produce or execute any attack payloads:
1. Attack strings in SKILL.md (e.g. curl | sh, npx skills add, rm -rf) are patterns AIShield matches as the scanned target, not instructions for the agent.
2. The ruleset (scanner/rules.py) is stored as static regex+severity and dispatched to the scanner engine at runtime — never interpreted as instructions by the agent.
3. The MCP server (npx aishield-mcp-server) is a pure HTTP client that sends audit requests to https://aishield.tools or a local API. No code execution surface.
4. The local scan path (scan_workspace.py) reads the filesystem only. No subprocess calls (this is the project's core invariant).

Upstream repo: https://github.com/lm203688/aishield (MIT)
Live API: https://aishield.tools
npm package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/aishield-mcp-server

Verification (run in a clean environment):
  curl -X POST https://aishield.tools/api/v1/audit \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"source_url":"https://github.com/owner/any-mcp-repo","tool_type":"mcp"}'
form._contact_email_note: Fill in your own email if the form asks for contact. Optional for public submission.
form._twitter_note: Optional. Only fill if you want to link an X/Twitter account.

common_rejection_reasons.rule_count_mismatch: curl https://aishield.tools/api/v1/health to get current rules_count, sync SKILL.md + README, resubmit.
common_rejection_reasons.classified_as_attack_tool: Re-emphasize the compliance statement in README §5 and in SKILL.md (mark attack strings as scanned targets).

official_marketplace_note: claude-plugins-official is Anthropic-curated manually. There is no application process. The submission form does NOT add plugins to the official marketplace. You get into the community marketplace first, then Anthropic may invite you once scale is demonstrated.

network_contingency.platform_claude_from_mainland: Redirects to app-unavailable-in-region. Requires overseas network egress (not just a proxy — platform.claude.com must classify you as being in a supported region).
network_contingency.alternative: Use claude.ai/admin-settings/directory/submissions/plugins/new if you have a Team/Enterprise account.
